output.brief: The rise in delayed alarm responses comes from the 12 August move of the alarm relay server to new hardware, not from agency staffing. The import skipped 11 of 14 forwarding rules. Those rules held back brief SpO2 dips, suppressed repeat alerts, and sent probe-off alarms only to the charge phone. Since then, phones in Pods A-C get about twice as many notifications per nurse, and acknowledgement takes about twice as long. Pod D still uses the old server and shows no change. Core, agency and new-graduate nurses all have similar rates in the affected pods, and Pod D has the same agency share with no rise. Bedside alarm volume was flat, which counts against heavier patient acuity and the monitor update. Sick leave may be linked to the alert overload, but that is unproven. I'm fairly confident, about 85-90%. Don't approve the agency cap or the performance reviews, since they would punish nurses for a system fault. Restore the 11 rules, with clinical validation and committee sign-off. Then track notifications per nurse and acknowledgement times weekly. Don't stop phone forwarding of SpO2 alarms, because the central station is unstaffed at night. Check phone coverage in Room 14 separately.
